# OPHTML 1.1.1 — complete starter context for LLMs

Repository: https://github.com/NasimiAsl/OPHTML
License: MIT, copyright 2026 NasimiAsl.
OPHTML means Over Powered HTML. It is a browser-only ES module with no runtime
package dependencies or build step. It combines HTML component rendering,
dyHTML-compatible templates, configurable style utilities, and animation CSS.
This document is framework context, not the user's app specification. Follow
it with the actual app request. Do not invent APIs that are absent below.

## Files and setup

Current runtime: dyHTML/ophtml.js (self-contained, including styles).
Legacy references: dyHTML/dyhtmlv2.0.01.js and dyHTML/dystyle.js; do not load them
in a new OPHTML app. Preserve existing application files when integrating.
Use modern browsers supporting ES modules, CSS media range queries, and Web
Animations. Serve over HTTP, e.g. python3 -m http.server 8000, not file://.

import OPHTML, { style } from './dyHTML/ophtml.js';
const _dy = OPHTML.html;
_dy.root = '/components/';
_dy.style.use({ colors: { brand: '#1462ab' } });
try {
  document.querySelector('#app').innerHTML = await _dy.render('welcome', {
    heading: 'Welcome', available: true
  });
} catch (error) {
  document.querySelector('#app').textContent = error.message;
}

Default export: { html, script, style }. Globals: _dy, _dyScript, _dyStyle,
_ophtml, _ophtmlScript, _ophtmlStyle. _dy.style === OPHTML.style === style.
Named ophtml is a legacy constructor alias of dy, not the default object.

## Paths and rendering

_dy.root = '/components/'; render('welcome') loads /components/welcome.htm.
render('shop.card') loads /components/shop/card.htm. Leading slashes in names
are stripped. Names may include .htm. A root without trailing slash works.
The default root is /dyhtml/components/ (lowercase). Set it explicitly.
_dy.root overrides per-loader path / loadPage root arguments.
_dy.basePath is separate: it controls the legacy $$root template placeholder.

- await _dy.render(page, params?, showData?) -> HTML string.
  Third argument true -> { html, data }; data.TID identifies component state.
  Parameters are shallow-copied; nested values remain references.
- await _dy.renderElement(element, page, params?, css?) -> generated div wrapper.
  Creates a controller, replaces target contents after successful render.
- await _dy.loadPage(page, controller?, callback?, root?, params?, after?)
  -> { html, data }. callback(controller, html, params) owns insertion if given;
  otherwise controller.innerHTML is assigned. after(params) follows background.
- await _dy.renderTemplate(template, data?, showData?) -> string or {html,data}.
  Ordinary text placeholders are filled from data, but initial conditions see
  wrapper parameters {data,TID}; use $$data.enabled in conditions here.
  Prefer file-based render for reusable/custom-tag-heavy components.

Templates are cached by resolved URL. params.noCache=true or 'true' refetches.
Request/template/init errors reject the render promise; use try/catch.
Await render waits for loading, header, async initialization, HTML callback,
and synchronous background code. It does NOT await custom-tag image-load hooks
or nested requests after insertion. Wait for their DOM to inspect readiness.

## Basic template syntax

Text placeholders: $$heading, $$price. Objects/arrays become internal JavaScript
references where needed (e.g. params="$$items"). Unknown placeholders remain.
Use distinct outer/item names: outer substitution runs before per-item work.
There is no universal nested-property text interpolation; flatten display
values or use #dy expressions. $$TID is the numeric component identity.
$$hide -> hdn-i; $$images -> /images; $$date -> timestamp.

#is value $$price > 100 #then
  <span>Premium</span>
#else
  <span>Standard</span>
#end

#if $$available #then <button>Buy</button> #end
#is define title <h1>$$title</h1> #else <h1>Untitled</h1> #end
#is not define description <p>No description</p> #end
<span>Total: #dy($$price * $$quantity#)</span>

#if aliases #is value. #then is required for expressions and optional for
define forms. #else is optional. Conditions nest; close every one with #end.
#is define checks legacy truthiness: null/undefined/false/empty/loosely zero
fail. #is not define checks only undefined (null is considered defined).
Expressions accept $$parameter, $$$item (current parameters/item), and trusted
JavaScript. Quoted legacy placeholders also work: "$$status" === "active".
Invalid expressions/unbalanced directives throw. Expressions are not sandboxed.

## Repeaters

Caller data: { heading:'Tasks', tasks:[{label:'Read',done:true}] }.
Component:

<h1>$$heading</h1>
<div class="f f-c gap-md">
  <repeater params="$$tasks">
    <article class="_p-md rad-md op-slide-up">
      <span>$$label</span>
      #_is value $$done #_then
        <span>Completed</span>
      #_else
        <span>Pending</span>
      #_end
      <span>Row #_dy($$repeaterIndex + 1#_)</span>
      <button onclick="console.log($$repeaterItem)">Inspect</button>
    </article>
  </repeater>
</div>

Use arrays of objects. Null/primitive entries are skipped, empty arrays render
empty. The hook replaces ALL content of its parent wrapper. Keep headings and
unrelated siblings outside that wrapper. Conditions/expressions for items MUST
be deferred with #_is/#_if, #_then, #_else, #_end, #_dy(EXPR#_).
Item fields become $$field. $$repeaterKey is collection key; $$repeaterIndex is
zero-based object-item index; $$repeaterItem is an original-object JS reference.
The engine adds repeaterKey/repeaterIndex to item objects. oncreate can transform
interpolated item HTML using content, data, index. For nested lists, repeat a
loader: <div><repeater params="$$groups"><div><loader page="category-list"
params="$$repeaterItem"></loader></div></repeater></div>. The child .htm component
can repeat its own $$entries array. This isolates template/data scopes. See
examples/gallery/components/nested-categories.htm and category-list.htm, plus
nested-board.htm -> board-column.htm -> board-card.htm for three levels. Avoid
directly nested repeater tags in a single template.

## Other custom tags

Use lowercase paired tags; these compile as strings, not Web Components.
Give consuming loader/repeater/switcher/content tags a dedicated wrapper.

<div><loader page="card" params="{name:'Ada'}"></loader></div>
<iloader page="card" params="{name:'Ada'}"></iloader>
<com "card" params="{name:'Ada'}"></com>
<div><content params="{name:'Ada'}">$$name</content></div>
<icontent params="{name:'Ada'}">$$name</icontent>
<dy "{name:'Ada'}">$$name</dy>
<div><dyc "{name:'Ada'}">$$name</dyc></div>

params is a trusted JavaScript expression, not necessarily JSON. Loader fields
include page, path, params, def, css, onready, online. def="false" removes parent.

<div>
  <switcher params="{loggedIn:true}" oncreate="item = data.loggedIn ? 1 : 0;">
    <p>Sign in</p>$$next-case<p>Welcome</p>
  </switcher>
</div>

Cases start at 0; default is 0; invalid case throws. No invented switch API.

## State, scripts and interaction

Use normal DOM events/delegation from your app JS for simple interactions.
There is no reactive state/binding system: update DOM or explicitly render again.
Initialization section in a .htm file:

<script>
  $$_clicks = 0;
  $$_increment = function(button) {
    $$_clicks += 1;
    button.textContent = 'Clicks: ' + $$_clicks;
  };
</script>
/// main content
<button onclick="_dy.TsID[$$TID].increment(this)">Clicks: 0</button>

In scripts $$_name maps to _dy.TsID[TID].name; $$$item maps to state. Initialization
may await and runs once per identity. Its data argument is state; state.ref is
render params. Every render creates a fresh identity. Plain inline markup does
not universally expand $$_; use explicit _dy.TsID[$$TID] references as shown.

Other script sections:
- /// header: preceding JS runs asynchronously with a fresh item object; its
  assigned properties merge into template params before condition evaluation.
  Header item is not the data argument from render.
- /// background script: following JS runs after the HTML callback through eval.
  $$_ctrl exists when a controller is supplied; plain render has none. No
  top-level await here; internally started promises are not awaited.

_dy.getDyElement(selectorOrElement) reads state only for an element with .iden,
not arbitrary descendants. State/ref collections have no public disposal API.

## Styling

_dy.style.use({
  colors: { brand:'#1462ab', surface:'#f5f7fb' },
  sizes: { card:'320px', space:'20px' },
  textSizes:{title:'28px'}, borders:{thin:'0.5px'}, radius:{card:'12px'},
  layers:{menu:50}, opacity:{muted:.6}, breakPoints:[420,720,1010]
});

use(options,id='ophtml-theme') merges objects with defaults and replaces that
style element; later calls start from defaults, not previous custom options.
init(css) appends a style element. live(id,css) updates/creates one. build(options)
returns utility CSS. Individual generators return strings without defaults:
size/fontSize/border/color/radius/layer/opacity/shadow/responsive(options), and
flex/nasted/nested/overflow/hidden/icon/animation(). nested aliases nasted.
_dyStyle is the integrated compatibility alias; do not import old dystyle.js.

Default sizes: 0=0px,xs=4px,sm=8px,md=16px,lg=24px,xl=32px,full=100%,auto=auto.
Default colors: main=#1462ab,white=#fff,black=#000,transparent=transparent.
Default text sizes: sm=12px,md=16px,lg=24px,xl=32px.
Default radius: 0=0px,sm=4px,md=8px,lg=16px,full=9999px.
Default borders: 0=0px,1=1px,2=2px. Default opacity: 0=0,05=.5,1=1.

For sizes token space:
_w-space/_h-space dimensions; _w-mn-space/_w-mx-space min/max width;
_h-mn-space/_h-mx-space min/max height; _w-ex-space/_h-ex-space exact dimension;
_p-space,_pl-space,_pr-space,_pt-space,_pb-space,_plr-space,_ptb-space padding;
m-space,ml-space,mr-space,mt-space,mb-space,mlr-space,mtb-space margins;
l-space,r-space,t-space,b-space position; l-nspace etc negative position;
gap-space,gap-x-space,gap-y-space gaps. Insert -i before token for important:
_w-i-space, _w-mx-i-space, _ptb-i-space, mtb-i-space. Numeric lengths become px.
asp-2x3 gives aspect-ratio:2/3 (all 1..4 combinations).

Flex: f/fl display; f-r/f-c/f-rr/f-cr direction; f-w/f-nw/f-wr wrap;
f-js/f-jc/f-je/f-ja/f-jb justify; f-as/f-ac/f-ae/f-at/f-al align items.
For brand color: cbrand background, c-tbrand text, c-bbrand border;
c-ibrand,c-t-ibrand,c-b-ibrand important. Hover: c-hbrand,c-t-hbrand,c-b-hbrand;
focus uses -f; important states use e.g. c-i-hbrand, c-t-i-fbrand.
fs-title/fs-i-title font size; fw-100/300/500/700/900; ta-left/center/right.
ba-thin/bt-thin/bb-thin/bl-thin/br-thin borders; b-solid/b-dash/b-dot/b-none.
rad-card and rad-r/l/t/b-card corners; ly-menu z-index; op-muted opacity.
full/relative/absolute/fixed positioning; owf/owf-x/owf-y overflow.
hdn/hdn-i hidden; disabled class disables pointer events. icon requires the
Material Symbols Outlined font separately. use() includes legacy Helvetica rules.

Shadows: shadow('soft',{shadows:['12.15']}) returns shadow-soft-12-15 and
shadow-hsoft-12-15 hover (12px blur, .15 alpha). Structured form:
shadow('card',{shadows:{raised:{blur:'12.5px',opacity:.2,x:0,y:4}}}) generates
shadow-card-raised. Inject generator output with live/init. use() uses main namespace.

Responsive default bit order is smallest->largest:
resp-1000 width<420, resp-0100 420<=width<720,
resp-0010 720<=width<1010, resp-0001 width>=1010, resp-1111 all ranges.
1 displays flex, 0 hides important. No overlap at boundaries.
responsive({key:'show-',breakPoints:[400,600,900]}) customizes prefix/thresholds.
Two-bit short/tall masks apply only below first width threshold; see docs/styles.md.

style.helpers.show(target,duration?) shows now, hides after optional milliseconds.
style.helpers.hide(target,duration?) hides now, restores after optional milliseconds.
First matching element/DOM element; null if missing; prior visibility timer cancels.

## Animations

Automatic CSS (no style.use needed):
op-fade-in/out, op-slide-up/down/left/right, op-zoom-in/out, op-pulse, op-shake,
op-spin. Use one effect class per element; wrappers can compose transforms.
Most run once at 300ms/ease-out/both fill. CSS spin loops at 1s/linear.
Modifiers: op-fast=150ms, op-slow=1s, op-loop=infinite, op-paused.
CSS variables: --op-duration, --op-delay, --op-easing, --op-repeat.
Legacy animated fadeIn/bounceIn/zoomIn/etc. classes remain available.

const motion = _dy.animate('#card', 'fadeIn', {duration:400});
if (motion) { await motion.finished; motion.cancel(); }

Returns native Animation or null for missing element. Not a promise. Accepts a
selector or DOM element. Effect names: fadeIn,fadeOut,slideUp,slideDown,slideLeft,
slideRight,zoomIn,zoomOut,pulse,shake,spin (dashed/op-prefixed names also work).
Third argument: milliseconds number or native timing options. JS defaults to
one iteration, even spin; set iterations:Infinity for loops, then cancel later.
Never await an infinite animation's finished promise. Cancellation of a running
animation rejects finished. cancel() releases retained styles. Reduced-motion
preference makes CSS near-instant once and JS zero-duration once.

## Requests and helpers

_dy.down(options) / _dy.upload(options) return XHR, use callbacks, not promises.
Options: url,type,data(upload),file(upload),timeout,begin(xhr),success(text),
error(cause),end(),progress(percent). Defaults GET/POST; successful 2xx/304.
Use native fetch if a promise API is preferred. Script loader is also callback
based; native ES imports are preferred for application modules.
element(selector,parent?) -> first/null; address(object,'a.b') -> value/undefined.

## Constraints and verification

Templates, expressions and scripts are trusted code, with raw interpolation.
Escape/sanitize untrusted content for HTML/attribute/URL contexts; never put
untrusted text into executable code. Legacy eval/inline hooks and global String
helpers remain; strict CSP needs adaptation. No SSR, JSX, automatic data binding,
or automatic reactive rendering is provided. Preserve existing APIs/workflow.

Runnable example: examples/store/index.html, main.js, components/catalog.htm.
36-example gallery: examples/gallery/index.html, samples.js, main.js, components/.
Each card exposes template (including dependencies), data, and handler source.
Gallery ctx.root/data/render/notify/setTheme are example scaffolding, NOT runtime
APIs. docs/gallery.md explains nested components and style-driven dark/light mode.
Full docs: README.md, docs/templates.md, docs/api.md, docs/styles.md,
docs/animations.md, docs/migration.md, docs/llm-prompt.md.
For repo tests: npm ci; npx playwright install chromium; npm run check; npm test.
Report actual verification; do not fabricate tests or claim nested DOM is ready
just because render resolved. Deliver complete files and HTTP serve commands.
